findings.finding: The grep acceptance criterion is a prose judgment rather than an exit-code check, and it conflicts with the ADR amendment that step 4 asks for. The search covers all of `src`, where 'sunset' legitimately appears many times (for example `src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py`), so the command always prints lines. 'Prints no line about the engine switch' then has to be decided by reading the output. Separately, step 4's 'dated 2026-11-12 amendment note recording the change of intent' will naturally name the earlier ticket `bossy-impish-hoiho` and/or the word 'sunset'. Those words would appear in `docs/adr/0123-selectable-plan-review-engine.md`, a file this grep scans.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: the `git grep -n -iE 'bossy-impish-hoiho|sunset' ...` line, versus Plan step 4
scenarios: The executor writes 'Supersedes the earlier sunset plan (bossy-impish-hoiho)' in the amendment note, and the AC appears to fail.

findings.finding: The [non-codebase] AC says bossy-impish-hoiho is closed with `--class obsolete`, but `obsolete` is a reason-required class. findings.finding: The plan says that, by the repo's convention, a permanent setting's marker names a 'standing admission ticket'. It cites docs/architecture.md §"Mechanism-delta ratchet" and src/rebar/_commands/sunset_markers.py for this. Neither source sets up such a convention. sunset_markers.py says an admission 'has to name a SUNSET TICKET' and calls the earlier permanent admission retired. Its close-refusal message tells the operator to 'repoint it at the ticket that will retire it'. docs/architecture.md and AGENTS.md describe only `<reason or ticket id>`. The phrase 'standing admission' appears nowhere in the repo. The marker passes lint because the grammar only checks shape, but the plan presents a new pattern as if it were already documented, and leaves the docs silent about it.
findings.location: Problem § 'Convention for admitting a mechanism added after the baseline froze' (third bullet); Plan step 1
scenarios: A later reviewer or contributor reads sunset_markers.py, sees cankered-cloistered-bittern is a ticket that is never meant to close, and treats it as the permanent rubber-stamp admission the grammar was written to prevent.
Another permanent mechanism needs admission, and with no documented pattern the next author either copies this one without a guide or invents a different one.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a step: in docs/architecture.md §"The marker", add a sentence saying that a permanent mechanism's marker names a standing admission ticket, which stays open as long as the mechanism exists and closes in the change that removes it. Give verify.plan_review_engine → cankered-cloistered-bittern as the example. Reword the Problem bullet to cite that new text instead of claiming the convention already exists.
